{{2013–14 ACC men's basketball standings}}

The '''2013–14 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team''' represented [[Syracuse University]] during the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games at the [[Carrier Dome]] in [[Syracuse, New York]]. This marked Syracuse's inaugural season in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]], having moved from the [[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]]. They finished the season 28–6, 14–4 in ACC play to finish in second place. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2014 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] to North Carolina State. They received an at-large bid to the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated Western Michigan in the second round before losing in the third round to Dayton. They started the season 25–0 before losing 6 of their final 9 games.

==Preseason==

===Roster changes===
Syracuse lost two major contributors to graduation, [[combo guard]] [[Brandon Triche]] and [[small forward]] James Southerland.  In addition, [[point guard]] [[Michael Carter-Williams]] left for the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].

Syracuse added five incoming freshmen including key contributor [[Tyler Ennis (basketball)|Tyler Ennis]], and [[swingman]] Michael Gbinije became eligible after sitting out the 2012-13 season because of NCAA transfer rules.

===Preseason outlook===

At ACC Media Days, members of the media voted [[C.J. Fair]] the preseason Player of the Year.  The media ranked SU the number two team in the conference behind [[2013–14 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cnycentral.com/sports/story.aspx?id=959518|publisher=[[CNY Central]]|date=October 16, 2013|title=Media votes C.J. Fair preseason ACC Player of Year, SU 2nd in conference |accessdate=2013-10-17}}</ref>

In its preseason rankings, The [[Sporting News]] ranked Syracuse eighth overall and second in the ACC behind Duke.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2013-09-10/college-basketball-top-25-sporting-news-preseason-rankings-2013-14-analysis/slide/8/|publisher=[[Sporting News]]|date=September 10, 2013|title=College basketball Top 25: Sporting News' preseason rankings for 2013-14|accessdate=2013-09-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130913004038/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2013-09-10/college-basketball-top-25-sporting-news-preseason-rankings-2013-14-analysis/slide/8|archive-date=2013-09-13|url-status=dead}}</ref>  TSN named C.J. Fair a third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].

[[Lindy’s Sports]] ranked Syracuse twelfth in its preseason ranking, third in the ACC behind Duke and [[2013–14 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/09/syracuse_ranked_no_8_in_the_sp.html|publisher=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=September 10, 2013|title=Syracuse basketball ranked No. 8 in The Sporting News; No. 12 in Lindy's|accessdate=2013-09-10}}</ref>  Lindy's named C.J. Fair its pre-season Player of the Year for the ACC.

[[Blue Ribbon College Basketball Yearbook]] ranked Syracuse eighth in its preseason ranking, second in the ACC behind Duke.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/09/syracuse_ranked_no_8_in_blue_r.html|publisher=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=September 17, 2013|title=Syracuse ranked No. 8 in Blue Ribbon Basketball Yearbook's Top 25 |accessdate=2013-09-17}}</ref>
